operation so enter mixture of experts which is a machine learning approach that divides an ai model into separate sub networks or experts each expert focuses on a subset of the input data and only the relevant experts areated for a given task rather than using the entire network for every operation now mixer experts isn't newnot at all it goes back to a paper published in99 ninety-one when researchers proposed an ai system with separate networks each specializing in different training and their experiment was a hit the model reached target accuracy in half the training cycles of a conventional model now fast forward to today and mixture of expertsis making a bit of a comeback it s kind of trendy again and leading large language models like ones from mistral are using it so let s break down the mixture of experts architecture let see what it s made of well we have in our model and input and and output now we also have a bunch of expert networks in between and there s probablymany of them i ll just draw a few so we ll have expert network number one expert network number two all the way through to expert network n and these sit between the input and the output now there is a thing called a gating network and this sits between the inputand the experts think of the gating network a bit like a traffic cop i guess deciding which experts should handle each sub task so we get a request in and the gating network will pick which experts it s going to invoke for that given input now the gating network assigns weight as it goes and with those weights we are using theresults combining them to produce the final output so we ll get the results back from those experts and combine them into our output here now we can think of the experts as specialized sub networks within the big and neural network and the gating network is acting as the coordinator activating only the best experts for each input so let s take a look at a real world example using that mistral model i mentioned earlier thatactuallycalled mixral and the specific name isral8 times7 b it s a large language model open source and in this model each layer has a total of8 experts each expert consists of 7 billion parameters that s what the7 b is which on its own is actually quite a small model for a large language model now as the model processes each token like a word or a part of a word a router network in each layer picks the two most suitable experts out of the eight and these two experts do their thing the outputs are mixed together and the combined result moves on to the next layer so let's take a look at some of the concepts that make up thisarchitecture and the first one i want to mention is called sparsearsity in a sparse layer only experts and their parameters that are activated from the list of all of themso we just select a few and this approach cuts down on compute needs as opposed to sending the request through the whole network andley is really shine when dealing with complex high dimensional data like for example human language so think about it different parts of a sentence might need different types of analysis you might need one expert that can understand idioms like it raining cats and dogs and then you might need another expert to untangle complex grammar structures so sparse mixture of expert models are great at this because they can call in just the right experts for each part of the input allowing for specialized processingnow another important concept is the concept of routingnow this refers to how this gating network here decides which expert to use and there are various ways to do this but getting it right is key if the routing strategy is off some expertsmight end up under trained or they might end up to specialized which can make the whole network less effective so here how routing typically works the router predicts how likely each expert is to give the best output for a given input this prediction is based on the strength of connections between the expert and the current data now mixral for example uses what is called a top k routing strategywhere k is the number of experts selected specifically it uses top two routing meaning it picks the best two out of its eight experts for each task now while this approach has his advantages it can also lead to some challenges and that leads us to our next concept and that is load balancing now in mixture of experts models there s apotential issue where the gating network it may converge to consistentlyate only a few experts and this creates a bit of a itself reinforcing cycle because if certain experts are selected early on they receive more training leading to more reliable outputs and consequently these experts are chosen moreently while others remain underutil utilized that s an balance that can result in a significant portion of the network becoming ineffective essentiallying into computational overhead now to solve this research has developed a technique specifically4 top k and it s called noisy top k gating and using noise noisy top k gating introduces gh and noise to the probability values predicted for each expertduring the selection process the controlled randomness promotes a more evenly distributed activation oferts so mixture of experts offers a bunch ofages in efficiency and performance but it s not without its challenges it introduces model complexityity which can make training more difficult and time consuming the routinging mechanism while powerful adds another layer ofacy to the model architecture and issues like load balancing and potential under utilization of experts require careful tuning and monitoring but still formany applications particularly large scale language models where computational resources are a premium the improved efficiency and specialized processing capabilities of the mixture of experts architecture make it a compelling option
